title: Declare an explicit cache policy on every response
statement: Each response class the site serves carries a deliberate Cache-Control value, so no response relies on a heuristic the origin, the edge, and the browser may each resolve differently.
rationale: With no directive present each layer applies its own default, which means the site's caching behaviour is decided by whichever intermediary is in the path rather than by the site.
implementation: Enumerate the response classes - document, hashed asset, unhashed asset, API payload, authenticated response - and set one directive per class in a single place. Do not add a directive per route where a class-level rule covers it.

verification.method: Request one representative URL per response class and record the Cache-Control, Expires, and Age headers returned at both the edge and the origin.

title: Serve versioned static assets under immutable directives
statement: An asset whose URL changes whenever its bytes change is served with a long maximum age and the immutable extension, and an asset served from a stable URL is not.
rationale: When the URL already encodes the content, revalidation can never find a difference, so every conditional request for it is a round trip spent confirming what the URL guaranteed.
implementation: Confirm the build emits a content hash in the asset filename before extending its lifetime, and apply the directive by path pattern so an unhashed asset cannot pick it up accidentally. Applying it to a stable URL makes the old bytes unretractable.

verification.method: Request built assets and confirm the long-lived directive applies only to URLs whose filenames contain a content hash.

title: Keep private responses out of shared caches
statement: Any response whose body depends on who is asking carries a directive forbidding shared storage, and no such response is served from an edge or proxy cache to a different requester.
rationale: A shared cache that stores one reader's personalised response will serve it to the next requester of that URL, which discloses their data through infrastructure rather than through any application flaw.
implementation: Set the private directive wherever the session influences the body, and confirm the edge honours it rather than assuming it does. Where personalisation is optional, serving a shared shell and fetching the personalised part separately keeps the document cacheable.

verification.method: Request an authenticated URL as one session, then request it again with no session through the same edge, and compare the bodies and the Age header.

sources.title: RFC 9111: HTTP Caching, storing responses in shared caches

title: Match document freshness to how often content changes
statement: The lifetime declared for an HTML document reflects how quickly its content becomes wrong, and a document whose content can change at any moment is revalidated rather than served from a long-lived copy.
rationale: A lifetime longer than the content's stability serves stale pages to readers and to crawlers with no signal that anything is out of date, and a lifetime of zero discards caching the site could have had.
implementation: Group documents by how volatile their content is and set a lifetime per group, using revalidation for the volatile group rather than a very short lifetime. Where the publishing system can purge on change, a longer lifetime plus purge is stronger than a guess.

verification.method: Publish a content change and measure how long the previous body continues to be served from the edge and from the browser.

title: Vary responses only on headers that change the body
statement: The Vary header names exactly those request headers the response body actually depends on, and no others.
rationale: Every header named multiplies the number of stored copies, so naming one the body ignores fragments the cache into variants that can never be reused, while omitting one the body does depend on serves the wrong variant.
implementation: Determine which request headers the response generation reads and name those. Where content negotiation is driven by a header the cache cannot see, redirect to a distinct URL per variant instead of varying on it.

verification.method: Request each URL with the named headers varied one at a time and confirm the body changes only for the headers listed.

caution: Varying on the user agent to serve different content to crawlers is not covered by this record and is addressed as a prohibited practice elsewhere in the registry.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics, the Vary field
